newsitem.title: USA: Montgomery Asset Management chief looks to expand.
newsitem.headline: Montgomery Asset Management chief looks to expand.

text.p: Stephen Doyle, founding chairman of Montgomery Asset Management, on Tuesday said his mutual fund operation could be enlarged through an acquisition after its sale to Commerzbank AG.
Doyle told Reuters in an interview Tuesday evening that the asset-management concern may want to add a small U.S. boutique firm specializing in value funds.
Earlier Tuesday, its parent, Montgomery Securities, a San Francisco-based investment banking firm, said it was selling the asset-management unit to Commerzbank.
"The Commerzbank agreement would give us an opportunity" to make such a deal, Doyle said. He cautioned that it was too soon to consider any acquisitions, as the Commerzbank deal has yet to close.
Doyle and 40 other Montgomery Asset Management employees own about one-third of the unit. Under the Commerzbank deal, the parent would receive an undisclosed amount of cash for its two-thirds stake.
Under the agreement, Doyle and other stakeholders would be permitted to increase their holding, he said, without providing details.
Doyle said he had not sought to sell the unit. Instead, he was approached by management at the parent, which wanted to raise capital to expand other businesses.

Doyle said the purchase by Commerzbank was a good fit because the German bank, which is the third largest in that country and the 26th-largest in the world in terms of assets, would permit the investment management firm to continue operating with an entrepreneurial style.
Doyle said he expected Commerzbank would encourage the firm's "independence, automony and ownership."
